text:
incident-bot: PAGER: oncall-sre, severity=P2 — AcmeCorp (enterprise, VPC, dedicated pool) reporting elevated TLS handshake latency to their App Gateway in us-west-2; websocket connect attempts timing out and clients are retrying aggressively. Link: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2765432109 :rotating_light:

oncall-sre: Acknowledged. Paging in SRE. Who's the Acme SE?

maria: nora-se is on Acme. Nora, can you confirm changes on their side?

nora-se: I'm here. Acme rolled out a config change at 05:12 UTC that bumped TLS min version checks and enabled stricter SNI validation on their edge. They say only streaming endpoints are failing, plain HTTP health checks are fine.

dave-platform: Observed spikes on handshake latency around 05:15 UTC. TLS handshake 95th percentile jumped from ~80ms -> 2.3s for connections to their AppGW IPs. Backend pool (dedicated-gw-prod-acme) shows connection backlog and `accept()` slowdowns.

kevin-se: Customer side logs show repeated client retries with short backoff (500ms) which amplifies the load. They are using a custom webclient that retries aggressively.

oncall-sre: TL;DR: TLS handshake slowness + aggressive client retries -> connection storms -> websocket timeouts. Impact: streaming sessions failing intermittently, retries causing cascading failures for their app.

maria: Steps to triage: 1) Confirm whether this is network (packet loss) vs CPU crypto pressure vs cert validation. 2) Check kernel TCP stats, openssl stats, and any mid-tier TLS terminator logs.

dave-platform: I ran quick checks: `ss -tan state SYN-SENT` shows elevated SYN retransmits to AppGW. `dmesg` shows no OOM or CPU steal. TLS worker threads show high per-thread latency. Could be CPU noisy neighbor or expensive crypto params (ECDSA with large curves).

maria: Can you paste the `nginx`/terminator TLS logs snippet?

dave-platform: Pasting tail from terminator logs:

```
[05:16:02] conn=1845 accepted tls handshake start, client=10.2.5.12
[05:16:03] tls: certificate verify: ok
[05:16:04] tls: handshake complete, cipher=ECDHE-ECDSA-AES128-GCM-SHA256, duration=2305ms
[05:16:05] conn=1846 accepted tls handshake start, client=10.2.5.20
```

maria: duration=2305ms — that matches. Cipher ECDHE-ECDSA: CPU heavy. Do we have hardware crypto offload?

oncall-sre: Dedicated pool nodes are NVMe + general purpose CPUs, no HSM. Suggest immediate mitigations: 1) Temporarily bump handshake timeout upstream so clients don't retry so quickly, 2) Offload some traffic to fallback region or different pool with less crypto contention, 3) Advise Acme to increase client backoff and/or switch to a less expensive cipher preference while we stabilize.

nora-se: I can ask Acme to push a client-side config to increase retry backoff to 2s within the next 10 minutes. They can also revert the strict SNI check as a short-term rollback.

kevin-se: On our side we can: - Add a graceful 503 on new streaming connections when worker queues are > threshold - Increase per-worker thread pool for TLS if safe - Temporarily prefer AES128 vs ECDSA if a cert fallback is possible.

maria: Let's do a minimal-impact mitigation first. Action items (live):
- oncall-sre: add a temporary connection admission filter rule to return 503 for new streaming upgrade requests when TLS worker latency > 1s. Command: `redwoodctl routes update --id dedicated-gw-prod-acme --admit-threshold 1s --on-overflow 503`
- dave-platform: spin up 2 warm nodes in dedicated-acme pool and attach to LB (scale +2).
- nora-se: request Acme to increase client retry backoff to 2s and consider reverting SNI strictness if they can.

oncall-sre: Executing admission filter now. `applied rule` — watching metrics.

dave-platform: Scaling nodes: `scale --pool dedicated-acme --delta 2` — nodes provisioning, ETA ~70s.

acme-ops-bot: Acme configured client backoff to 2s at 05:19:13 UTC. Rolling out to 30% of clients.

kevin-se: Observing immediate drop in new conn attempts per second from the client side (expected). Handshake latency p95 dropping from 2.3s -> 900ms within 30s. Good signal.

maria: Any errors from LB about TLS limits?

dave-platform: LB reports handshake queue length flattened. However websocket upstream timeouts still occur for sessions that were mid-handshake during the spike. We'll gradually drain those.

nora-se: Acme prefers we avoid full region failover. Their compliance team won't allow cert changes. So keep mitigations at admission + client backoff + scale.

oncall-sre: Noted. I'm updating the incident doc: https://incidents.redwood/INC-2765432109 — adding current mitigations and timeline.

maria: Follow-ups: 1) Run `strace` on a slow worker to see where time goes. 2) Check CPU crypto stats: `openssl speed` vs current cipher. 3) Add long-term: evaluate enabling CPU crypto acceleration or swapping to ECDHE-RSA if cert allows.

kevin-se: I captured a `strace` sample: shows time in `SSL_do_handshake` and waiting on `poll()`. Looks CPU-bound inside the TLS handshake.

oncall-sre: Customer impact: intermittent streaming disconnects for ~8% of sessions in the 05:15-05:22 UTC window. No data exfiltration. Severity remains P2.

maria: After scale + client backoff + admission filter, metrics are steady. p95 handshake now ~420ms. We'll keep changes for 30 minutes and monitor. Nora, coordinate with Acme for a postmortem call and ask them to consider changing client retry logic permanently.

nora-se: Will do. I'll schedule a follow-up and include test plan to simulate aggressive retries.

oncall-sre: Handoff: I will remain on this thread for 30 mins. If things re-escalate, escalate to eng-runtime (kevin-se + dave-platform).

incident-bot: NOTE: Paging silence for incident responders set until 06:00 UTC. Incident updated: status=mitigated, followup_required=true.

maria: Thanks team. Logging the mitigations in the incident timeline and creating a ticket to evaluate cipher policy across dedicated pools.

kevin-se: Added runbook item to consider TLS worker autoscaling based on handshake latency and to evaluate hardware accelerators for crypto.

oncall-sre: Closing live mitigation loop. Leaving the thread open for postmortem notes. :white_check_mark:
